# Insurance startup Corgi reportedly raised more money at $4B — its third round in 8 weeks
[Julie Bort](https://techcrunch.com/author/julie-bort/)

1:13 PM PDT · July 23, 2026

[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F07%2F23%2Finsurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks%2F)[Share on X](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F07%2F23%2Finsurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks%2F&text=Insurance+startup+Corgi+reportedly+raised+more+money+at+%244B+%E2%80%94+its+third+round+in+8+weeks&via=techcrunch)[Share on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F07%2F23%2Finsurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks%2F&title=Insurance+startup+Corgi+reportedly+raised+more+money+at+%244B+%E2%80%94+its+third+round+in+8+weeks&summary=In+the+AI-funding+frenzy%2C+many+startups+are+raising+back-to-back+rounds+at+ever-increasing+valuations+%E2%80%94+but+even+by+those+standards%2C+Corgi+stands+out.&mini=1&source=TechCrunch)[Share on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/submit?url=https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F07%2F23%2Finsurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks%2F&title=Insurance+startup+Corgi+reportedly+raised+more+money+at+%244B+%E2%80%94+its+third+round+in+8+weeks)[Share over Email](mailto:?subject=Insurance+startup+Corgi+reportedly+raised+more+money+at+%244B+%E2%80%94+its+third+round+in+8+weeks&body=Article%3A+https%3A%2F%2Ftechcrunch.com%2F2026%2F07%2F23%2Finsurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks%2F)[Copy Share Link](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/23/insurance-startup-corgi-reportedly-raised-more-money-at-4b-its-third-round-in-eight-weeks/)

Insurance tech, data room software, and coffee-shop startup Corgi is reportedly raising yet another round that closely follows its last raise and would double its valuation, [sources have told Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/annatong/2026/07/22/ai-startup-corgi-of-seven-day-work-week-fame-raises-yet-again-at-4-billion-valuation/?utm_source=ForbesMainTwitter&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ForbesMainTwitter).

The round is said to be a second extension of its Series B round and has already closed. Corgi announced its last round, the B1 round of $106 million at a $2.6 billion valuation at the end of May, about eight weeks ago.

In the AI-funding frenzy, many startups are raising back-to-back rounds at ever-increasing valuations — but even by those standards, Corgi stands out.

The Y Combinator alum (summer 2024) [raised a $108 million Series A](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/corgi-raises-108m) in January at an undisclosed valuation. (PitchBook estimates $630 million post-money.) Four months later, in early May, it [raised its Series B](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/06/insurance-startup-corgi-hits-1-3b-valuation-4-months-after-its-series-a/): $160 million at a $1.3 billion valuation. Just three weeks later, it announced a B1 round from the same investors, saying they’d invested $106 million at a $2.6 billion valuation.

Now, eight weeks later, sources tell Forbes there’s a B2. Forbes did not report the amount of money that Corgi raised, though, and the company declined to comment on the potential funding.

Corgi is backed by TCV and Kindred Ventures. Kindred’s Kanyi Maqubela [cited the startup’s momentum](https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/28/corgi-announces-106m-raise-at-2-6b-valuation-three-weeks-after-160m-series-b/) to TechCrunch as justification for the last valuation leap. The apparent justification for the new valuation is the startup’s revenue trajectory.

When Corgi announced its Series A seven months ago, the founders said their company had already [hit $40 million in annualized revenue run rate](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/y-combinator_corgi-is-coming-out-of-stealth-with-a-total-activity-7415090061496586241-N0MX/). Sources told Forbes it’s now on track to increase run rate to $450 million by the end of the year.

Corgi offers AI-powered insurance. It uses AI to give prospects fast quotes and [to speed payments on claims](https://www.corgi.insure/blog/claims-experience-full-stack-carrier). It offers startups various types of liability insurance like general liability, coverage of tech-related incidents, and employment liability, as well as business renters’ and auto insurance.

Insurance is an inherently cash-intensive business but perhaps even more so for Corgi because it uses a type of insurance structure known as a Risk Retention Group (RRG). This is a way for people in the same industry, or those facing similar liabilities, to pool their resources and self-insure collectively.

Corgi has adopted some different structures for different types of insurance, however, a spokesperson says. In addition to RRGs, some policies might use state-regulated carriers, for instance.

If the claims are big enough, [they can even bankrupt the RRG](https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/east/2025/04/28/821485.htm).

Perhaps it’s not surprising, then, that Corgi wants to grow its coffers.

But even as the startup has expanded the types of insurance it offers, it has also branched out in other ways.

Plus, the startup operates two 24-hour coffee shops with cute and sometimes ad-sponsored drink names like “Brexspresso.” Opening up physical cafe locations also requires cash.
